rationale: The startup account still carries a stated gap: the with-snapshot control restarted a real prefix whose replay was zero batches, so the region where a snapshot shortens the replay without eliminating it was inferred rather than observed. This experiment produces real prefixes in that region. A single-node cluster commits 200 commands, takes a snapshot, then commits a second batch and shuts down, so the restart replays only the gap after the snapshot. With a 200-command second batch the gap is about 198 entries, four FSM batches at the default MaxAppendEntries=64, and NewRaft should return; with an 8300-command second batch the gap is about 8300 entries, 130 batches, and NewRaft should block. A local probe matched both predictions: the short case returned in 1 ms after four batches, the long case never returned within five seconds with one goroutine in processLogs. The formal run is requested so the shortened-replay region rests on a retained receipt.

scope.description: A real single-node cluster with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled commits a first batch of commands, takes a snapshot, commits a second batch, and shuts down. Both stores are retained, so the restart's replay is the difference between the staged commit index and the snapshot index. The short case uses 200 then 200 commands, which leaves a gap of roughly 198 entries or four FSM batches at MaxAppendEntries=64; the long case uses 200 then 8300, which leaves about 8300 entries or 130 batches. Each restart is started on a separate goroutine and bounded, and the events record the snapshot index, staged commit index, last log index, replay entries and batches, whether NewRaft returned, the elapsed time, the error and the number of goroutines left in processLogs.
assumptions: The snapshot taken between the two batches is durable in the in-memory snapshot store and is the newest snapshot on restart, so the replay starts after it.
The leader stages a commit index at the pre-dispatch index, so the staged commit index is the entry count rather than the last log index; the harness reports both so the gap can be recomputed.
A constructor that has not returned within the five-second window is treated as having made no progress.
excluded: No multi-node cluster and no snapshot taken during the replay.
Only MaxAppendEntries=64, the default; the boundary was sampled at other batch sizes by earlier receipts.
No attempt to shut down a node whose constructor never returned.

experiment.prefix: The harness bootstraps a single-voter configuration, starts one raft with 50 ms timeouts and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, waits up to ten seconds for leadership, applies the first batch of commands with five-second futures, calls Snapshot(), applies the second batch, reads the newest snapshot index from the snapshot store, reads the staged commit index and last log index from the log store, and shuts the node down. It then computes the replay as the staged commit index minus the snapshot index and the batch count as ceil(replay/MaxAppendEntries) and emits rc_case_<case> with the mode, the option flag, the batch sizes, the snapshot index, the staged commit index, the last log index, the replay entries and batches and the observation timeout. It then starts NewRaft on a fresh transport over the retained stores in a goroutine and waits up to the configured timeout. On return it shuts the node down; on timeout it records that no return was observed and leaves the node alone. It emits rc_result_<case> with the same identifiers, the batch parameters, returned, elapsed_ms, error and the change in the number of goroutines whose stack contains processLogs.
experiment.responsibility: Restarting from a snapshot plus a tail of committed entries is the normal recovery path for this option, and the library must complete it whenever the tail fits within the replay's dispatch capacity. The experiment measures that path with a real prefix rather than a seeded store, so the recovery region between a zero-length replay and a blocked one is observed instead of inferred.
semantic_changes: The prefix now takes its snapshot between two batches of commands instead of after all of them, so the replay is shortened rather than eliminated.
The short case's replay is four batches, which is the region earlier receipts left inferred.
Every result event records the snapshot index, staged commit index and replay arithmetic so the gap can be recomputed from the receipt.

comparisons.description: A real restart whose snapshot leaves a short tail must let NewRaft return.
The short case must actually replay a non-zero tail, so that it exercises the shortened-replay region rather than the zero-replay control.
The same recovery path with a tail past 128 batches must still let NewRaft return; the harness records that it does not.
